Note::NlpAccessor::intersect_tokens¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::NlpAccessor::intersect_tokens(const Note& other) const

Shared Words Between Two Notes¶

intersect_tokens(other) reduces each cell of self and the matching cell of other to a set of words, then returns the words present in both as a TokenBatch. It is the word-level member of the set-similarity family; the scoring members are jaccard_tokens and overlap_tokens, and the other set kinds are intersect_terms, intersect_acronyms, intersect_citations, and intersect_symbols.

How the set is built¶

Each cell is tokenized with the ASCII word tokenizer (the one tokens uses) and every token is lowercased. There is no length or stopword filter — for a content-word set that ignores the, and, with, and other function words, use intersect_terms. The set is deduplicated and case-folded, so a word that occurs many times counts once and FOX and fox are the same member.

What is emitted¶

For each cell pair, intersect_tokens emits the members that appear in both sets, in the order they first appear in self, once each. A cell whose two sets share nothing contributes an empty range.

The TokenBatch result¶

Shared words from all cells are concatenated into the rank-1 Note batch.tokens(). The rank-1 Int64 Note batch.offsets() has length numel + 1 and marks each cell’s run, so cell r owns tokens.at(k) for k in [offsets[r], offsets[r + 1]).

Shape, pairing, and rejections¶

The comparison is per cell and pairwise. self and other must have the same numel, or one may be a scalar (numel() == 1) broadcast against every cell of the other. Unlike the scoring members, intersect_tokens always returns a flat TokenBatch, not a shaped Note. Rejections raise pluss::Error:

  • either side in bytes mode → Note::NlpAccessor::intersect_tokens requires a UTF-8 text Note (lhs is bytes) (or rhs is bytes).

  • unequal numel with neither side a scalar → Note::NlpAccessor::intersect_tokens expects equal numel or scalar broadcast.

Example 1: Shared Words, Per Cell¶

const auto batch =
    pluss::make_note({"the quick brown fox", "alpha beta gamma"})
        .nlp().intersect_tokens(pluss::make_note({"a quick red fox", "beta gamma delta"}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["quick", "fox", "beta", "gamma"]
offsets: [0, 2, 4]

Cell 0 shares quick and fox (tokens()[0..2)); cell 1 shares beta and gamma (tokens()[2..4)).

Example 2: Deduplicated, In self Order, Case-Folded¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"fox fox dog cat fox"})
                       .nlp().intersect_tokens(pluss::make_note({"cat FOX"}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["fox", "cat"]

fox appears three times in self but once in the result, before cat because it is seen first; FOX in other matches it after case-folding.

Example 3: Scalar Broadcast¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"cat dog", "dog bird"})
                       .nlp().intersect_tokens(pluss::make_note({"dog"}));

std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["dog", "dog"]
offsets: [0, 1, 2]

Example 4: Nothing In Common¶

const auto batch = pluss::make_note({"one two"})
                       .nlp().intersect_tokens(pluss::make_note({"three four"}));
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets().integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
offsets: [0, 0]
